clue.text: Second most holy virtue?

parts.note: plays on the proverb that a certain virtue is next to godliness, so it ranks just behind the holiest of all

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says this habit of keeping washed and tidy is next to godliness, so it comes second in holiness.

clue.text: Calumny, in brief, I shall be resorting to

indicators.note: resorting means sorting again, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: I shall be, said briefly, is the contraction I'll be

explanation.surface: A promise to fall back on slander, put in a nutshell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in brief' shortens I shall be to I'LL BE, and 'resorting to' rearranges ILLBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and damaging statement, as is a written defamation.

clue.text: Draw two-wheeler up, in race

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Draw two-wheeler up, in race': TT (race) round reversed CART gives TTRACT, but no clue word supplies the opening A of ATTRACT (perhaps 'in a race' in the original)

clue.text: Doesn't eat spinach for example

definitions.meaning: a diner who abandons the food on the plate does not eat it
spinach is a vegetable eaten as foliage

explanation.surface: A child refuses greens.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abandons food on the plate does not eat it, and spinach is green foliage.

clue.text: There's no shortage of talent around fashionable Middle-East king

definitions.note: a phrase used for an adjective meaning plentiful

indicators.note: the sense word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: nous is practical intelligence or know-how
U means upper-class, hence posh or fashionable
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A trendy Gulf monarch is surrounded by plenty of gifted people.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: When things are many there is plenty of them, so no shortage.

clue.text: Patient attention required from such relatives?

definitions.text: Patient attention required from such relatives?

parts.words: Patient attention required from such relatives?
parts.note: patient means a hospital case, and a senior nurse in Britain carries the title of a female family member

explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a senior nurse is called Sister, a word also naming female siblings.

clue.text: Impersonator handing out cards, aiming to deceive

parts.note: a double is a lookalike who stands in for someone
dealing is distributing cards to players

explanation.surface: A card sharp in disguise cheats at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicitous behaviour sets out to trick and mislead people.

clue.text: Drive from abode to factory down under?

parts.note: Dis is the underworld of Roman myth, the abode of the dead, which 'down under' points to
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: Being moved out of home to an Australian works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' looks like Australia but places the abode below ground: Dis, the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb for uprooting, to expel someone from their place.

clue.text: Decline a copy — a faulty source of information

indicators.note: a faulty arrangement of letters needs to be put right, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refusing a flawed reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges DECLINEACOPY, and the second A ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A comprehensive reference book is a source of information on many subjects.

clue.text: Alternative piece or track

parts.note: the word or introduces an alternative
a bit is a piece of something

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between a spare part and a stretch of railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet's orbit is the path or course it follows round the sun.

clue.text: Entry of guilt?

parts.note: entry means being let in, but the phrase also suggests confessing to a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both being allowed in and a confession, as in owning up to guilt.

clue.text: A stag party with dancing first, then a pop singer

indicators.note: these words put the dancing party at the front, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a ball is a formal party with dancing
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A stag do that starts with a dance before a pop star turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of ballads, simple popular songs, is a pop singer of a sort.

clue.text: Lacks occupation

parts.note: reads like someone out of work, but describes a house or room with nobody living in it

explanation.definitionFit: A vacant building has no occupants, so it lacks occupation in the residential sense.

clue.text: New York time difference creating ill will

indicators.note: a difference made to the letters signals that they are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Jet lag between New York and home causes bad tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difference' turns NYTIME into the answer; the time difference of the surface is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or animosity between people is ill will.

clue.text: Stamina I'm developing, providing rigging for a dandy

indicators.note: developing letters change their form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters, with one I too many

explanation.surface: A fop gaining strength gets new clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges STAMINA plus M; the I of I'm is one letter too many. A dandy is also a small sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a small sailing boat, and its principal mast carries rigging.

clue.text: Pop takes everyone to this place in Saskatchewan

parts.note: to pop a balloon is to burst it
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Dad takes the whole family off to a Canadian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like Dad, but it is the verb. Saskatchewan is a Canadian prairie province.
explanation.definitionFit: Burstall is a small town in the Canadian province of Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Scandalised by tour adapted for pensioners?

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of tour are rearranged

parts.note: the aged are elderly people, such as pensioners

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by a coach trip designed for the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply offended or shocked by something is scandalised.

clue.text: Literary supplement?

parts.note: suggests a newspaper's books section, but means a section added at the close of a book or play

explanation.definitionFit: A closing section added after the main text of a book or play supplements the work.

clue.text: Duck requires orange sauce, then seasoning

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

indicators.note: sauce suggests cheeky liberties taken with the letters of orange, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Duck à l'orange followed by herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean herb used to flavour food is a seasoning.

clue.text: Capital bit of advice given to political leader

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint or bit of advice

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of political

explanation.surface: A party chief receives a useful hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city, but here it is the old exclamation of approval meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned British words for excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Trendy fruit drink — sound sense for person in the club

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: cider is a drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A fashionable cocktail and good judgment win acceptance in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an inner circle, one on the inside of a group.

clue.text: Hint Jack's heavy tackle should end this game

indicators.note: these words place the tackle at the finish of the answer

parts.note: a tip is a hint
Jack is a sailor, and a cat is the heavy tackle used to hoist a ship's anchor

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a sailor's gear should finish a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (as in Jack Tar) is a sailor in crosswords. The game is an old pastime of striking a tapered piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is a traditional game in which a small tapered stick is struck with a bat.

clue.text: Although avoiding extremes, plummet, with exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: avoiding the extremes of the word plummet means dropping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in shock as something falls sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping P and T from plummet leaves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British interjection, a corruption of 'Lord love me', expressing surprise.

clue.text: Guide lines the art gallery put back

parts.note: reins are the lines used to guide a horse
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Instructions for rehanging pictures in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries, chiefly in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former place is to put it back.

clue.text: Morning round no good when in company

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bad round of golf in the morning with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amid others is to be in their company.

clue.text: Home sick, clings to a doctor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A homesick patient hangs on to the GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb meaning tamper, not the physician the surface suggests; 'Home sick' is split to mean longing for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wistfully longing for home and the past feels homesick.

clue.text: Cunningly hid some books inside this garment

indicators.note: the books go inside the rearranged letters of hid
done cunningly, the letters of hid are shifted into a crafty new order

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone smuggles books in the folds of their clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' turns HID into DHI, and 'inside' puts OT within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The loincloth worn by many Hindu men in India is this garment.

clue.text: Where best to keep legs a doctor dissected

indicators.note: something dissected is cut apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A grisly note on where to store limbs after an autopsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrigerated storage is the best place to keep perishable things.
